definition: Delegated authorization: Google grants this app selected permissions without sharing the user password.
A token-based session representation managed by Auth.js; this app puts owner identity in its callbacks.
The authenticated application identity; distinct from the refresh credential needed to send Gmail.
A server-held credential used to obtain an access token; persisted encrypted in this implementation.
A temporary provider credential prepared explicitly before the final send claim.
A named permission in the Google consent grant, such as gmail.send.
A present-tense decision about whether an owner may use a feature, based on policy and current state.
Repeated use of the same operation identity returns the same result or avoids repeating its effect.
An owner-scoped UUID used to identify one campaign submission or checkout operation.
A stored copy of approved values, so later contact/template edits do not change a queued message.
The standard message format for text, HTML, headers and attachments; buildMime encodes it for Gmail.
A URL-safe base64 encoding used for the raw Gmail MIME message.
A stable message header identity; it is not proof of provider deduplication.
Durable local intent committed before publication to an external work system.
A durable provider-event receipt stored before asynchronous processing.
An HTTP callback from a provider. This app verifies Dodo signatures rather than requiring a user session.
Comparing/rebuilding local evidence and provider observations, including repairing interrupted publication.
A time-bounded claim on active work. Expiry does not prove the external effect did not happen.
An unpredictable identity tying settlement to the exact claimed attempt.
Durable accounting capacity assigned to a delivery before external submission.
Coordinated Universal Time, used for daily usage boundaries and documented cron schedules.
A time range including its start and excluding its end, preventing overlap at boundaries.
A verified extension of paid operational access that retains the same allowance identity.
Deny or defer protected work when required authorization/accounting controls are unavailable.
An owner whose data and operations must remain separate from other users.
A PostgreSQL transaction lock that serializes competing changes to the selected owner or budget.
A database unit whose local changes commit together or roll back together; external provider calls are outside it.
The typed database client and schema/migration tooling used by this application.
The Next.js route organization used for layouts, pages, loading/error boundaries and handlers.
A server-executed mutation entrypoint invoked by the UI; it still needs authentication and policy checks.
An HTTP endpoint implemented in an App Router route file.
A React component rendered on the server; it can prepare data without making all UI code client-side.
A React component opting into browser interactivity with use client.
The event/workflow orchestration library registering the app’s eight background functions.
An orchestration work boundary recorded by Inngest; replay semantics differ from another Gmail request.
A schedule expression used by periodic maintenance registrations.
Authenticated encryption used for refresh-token envelopes, with a random IV and integrity tag.
Additional authenticated data binding a v2 credential to its version, key ID, purpose and owner UUID.
The random initialization value used by encryption; v2 uses 12 bytes.
Update only if an observed old value still matches, preserving concurrent reconnect/erasure changes.
A retained deletion marker that blocks unsafe recreation or activation while cleanup is pending.
The signature/timestamp verification protocol used on the exact raw Dodo request body.
Integer currency subunits; configured examples include USD 599 and INR 29900.
A configuration or persisted control preventing activation before readiness is established.
A request-frequency budget; separate from daily/monthly email allowance and Gmail provider limits.
A delivery state where provider acceptance cannot be established; accounting remains and auto-resend is blocked.
A relation deletion behavior preserving the dependent record while clearing its foreign key.
A relation deletion behavior removing dependent records, used for owner content but not every recovery record.
Prebuilt HTML and assets served without an application server; used by this handbook.
